title: DA plans P18B budget for agri mechanization in 2027 to boost production
summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) said on Monday that it is eyeing up to P18 billion in the 2027 budget for agricultural machinery.

blocks.text: The Department of Agriculture (DA) said on Monday that it is eyeing up to P18 billion in the 2027 budget for agricultural machinery.

Most of the government’s budget for mechanization is under the Rice Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (RCEF), including the P9 billion allotted for rice machinery. But the DA is seeking a bigger allocation for farm machinery for other crops.

“But of course, the Department of Agriculture through its other programs also have machineries. I would safely assume we can easily almost double that,” said DA Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. in a press briefing during the Asia Pacific Conference on Sustainable Agricultural Mechanization.
“So we might have about P15 to 18 billion for 2027 available for farm machinery and motor vehicles,” he added.
The Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization (PhilMech) said that an additional P50 billion is needed to fully mechanize the rice sector alone.
“In the span of six years, we only mechanized around 60 % to 70% of our rice. So we're still needing 30% more,” said PhilMech director Dionisio Alvindia in the press briefing.
“That could value around P50 billion more to mechanize the whole system,” he added.

The Philippine government is pushing for accessible and sustainable mechanization of the agriculture sector to boost production, without leaving small farmers behind despite the modernization efforts.

“Modernization must be practical, accessible, and responsive to the realities of our farmers. It requires appropriate technologies, affordable financing, supportive policies, reliable after-sales services, and just as importantly, the skills to operate and maintain these machineries,” said Tiu Laurel Jr.
Meanwhile, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) noted that farmers will only invest in technologies that will boost their income.

“Farmers are some of the most innovative, risk-taking individuals that you will ever meet. But when we think about the evolution of technology and adoption of it, a farmer will not invest in a new technology unless she knows that it saves her money or helps her make a profit,” said FAO Deputy Director General Beth Bechdol in the press briefing.
However, the DA assured that mechanization of the agriculture sector won’t mean replacing farmers or any other human force in the sector.
“Machines should make farmers more productive, not make farmers irrelevant,” said Tiu Laurel Jr. —LDF, GMA News
